tb-E201-2.question:
An electron absorbs a photon and escapes from a metal of work function ϕ. Which of the following statements must be correct?

(1) The energy required by the electron to escape from the metal is ϕ.

(2) The electron gains an energy ϕ after absorbing the photon.

(3) All the energy of the photon is transferred to the electron.

A (2) only

B (3) only

C (1) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-E201-2.reasoning:
Different electrons need different amounts of energy to escape from a material.

∴ (1) is not necessarily correct.

tb-E201-3.question:
When a photon travels from air into water, its energy

A increases.

B decreases.

C remains unchanged.

D changes depending on the angle of incidence.
tb-E201-3.reasoning: The frequency f of the light remains unchanged when it travels from air to water. Therefore, the energy hf of the photon also remains unchanged.

tb-E201-4.question:
In the photoelectric effect experiment, light of frequency f is directed onto the cathode in the photocell. The p.d. V between the cathode and the anode is varied and the photoelectric current I is measured. The graph below shows how I changes with V (Fig a).

Which of the following statements is/are correct?

(1) The threshold frequency is higher than f.

(2) No photoelectron is emitted from the cathode when V is 1.8 V.

(3) The maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons emitted is 1.8 eV.

A (2) only

B (3) only

C (1) and (2) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-E201-4.reasoning:
f must be higher than the threshold frequency since there is photoelectric current.

∴ (1) is incorrect.

When V = 1.8 V, photoelectrons are still emitted from the cathode but all of them cannot overcome the p.d. across the photocell to reach the anode.

∴ (2) is incorrect.

source.name: E201 Revision 1 Particle Nature of Light.docx

A There is a shorter time delay for X to emit photoelectrons.

B There is a shorter time delay for Y to emit photoelectrons.

C If the frequency of the light source is reduced gradually, X will stop emitting photoelectrons first.

D If the frequency of the light source is reduced gradually, Y will stop emitting photoelectrons first.

tb-E201-6.question:
Metal plates X and Y are illuminated by a beam of violet light and a beam of green light respectively. The two light beams have the same intensity. Photoelectrons are emitted from both plates. Which of the following statements are correct?

(1) More photons reach plate Y than plate X per unit time per unit area.

(2) The kinetic energy of a photoelectron emitted from plate Y is always lower than that from plate X.

(3) Photoelectrons can still be emitted if the intensities of both light beams are reduced.

A (1) and (2) only

B (1) and (3) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-E201-6.reasoning:
By intensity = NhfAt ,

for the same intensity, f ↑ ⇒ NAt ↓

∴ (1) is correct.

Photoelectrons from the same metal plate are emitted with different KE.

∴ (2) is incorrect.

source.name: E201 Revision 1 Particle Nature of Light.docx

tb-E201-7.question:
In the photoelectric effect experiment, either the frequency or the intensity of the incident light is varied. The photoelectric current and the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons emitted are recorded. A graph is then obtained (Fig b).

Which of the following is/are the possible quantities represented by x and y?

x

intensity of incident light

(2)

(3)

tb-E201-8.question:
When a metal surface is illuminated separately by red, yellow and violet lights, photoelectrons with maximum kinetic energies KR, KY and KV are emitted respectively. If the same metal surface is illuminated by these coloured lights at the same time, what is the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons emitted?

A KR

B KV

C KR+KY+KV

D 13(KR+KY+KV)
tb-E201-8.reasoning: A photon of violet light possesses a higher energy than photons of red and yellow light. Also, each electron can only absorb one photon. When the metal surface is illuminated by the three coloured lights, an electron gains the maximum energy when it absorbs a violet light photon. Therefore, the maximum KE of the photoelectrons is KV.

source.name: E201 Revision 1 Particle Nature of Light.docx

tb-E201-9.question:
A photocell is connected to the power supply as shown (Fig c).

Monochromatic light is directed onto the cathode. The frequency of the light is higher than the threshold frequency of the cathode. However, no current is detected in the circuit. Which of the following changes may produce a current?

(1) Set the e.m.f. of the power supply to zero.

(2) Use monochromatic light of a higher intensity.

(3) Use monochromatic light of a shorter wavelength.

A (1) only

B (3) only

C (1) and (2) only

D (1) and (3) only
tb-E201-9.reasoning:
Initially, the anode repels photoelectrons. Setting the e.m.f. to zero removes this repelling force.

∴ (1) is correct.

Increasing the intensity of the light does not increase the energy of each photon.

∴ (2) is incorrect.

When wavelength decreases, the energy of each photon increases.

∴ (3) is correct.

source.name: E201 Revision 1 Particle Nature of Light.docx

tb-E201-10.question:
A photocell is connected to a variable power supply. Monochromatic light is incident on the cathode of the photocell so that photoelectrons are emitted. Which of the following does not affect the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons reaching the anode of the photocell?

A The material of the cathode

B The frequency of the light

C The intensity of the light

D The output voltage of the power supply
tb-E201-10.reasoning: The output voltage of the power supply affects the amount of energy gained or lost by a photoelectron during its travel from the cathode to the anode.

tb-E201-11.question:
Violet light of frequency 7.3 × 1014 Hz and intensity 0.05 W m–2 is directed onto the cathode of a photocell. If the area of the cathode surface receiving the violet light is 6.00 × 10−4 m2 and one electron is emitted for every 200 photons hitting the surface, find the maximum photoelectric current.

A 4.96 × 10–8 A

B 1.5 × 10–7 A

C 4.53 × 10–7 A

D 9.94 × 10–6 A
tb-E201-11.reasoning:
By intensity = NhfAt ,

0.05 = Nt × (6.63 × 10–34)(7.3 × 1014)6.00 × 10–4

Nt = 6.20 × 1013 s–1

Maximum photoelectric current

= 6.20 × 1013200 × (1.6 × 10−19)

= 4.96 × 10–8 A

tb-E201-12.question:
Figure d shows the maximum kinetic energy Kmax of the photoelectrons emitted by metals X and Y when the plates are illuminated by monochromatic lights of different wavelengths λ.

Which of the following statements are correct?

(1) No photoelectron is emitted if monochromatic light of wavelength 7.0 × 10–7 m is shone on metal X.

(2) If monochromatic light of wavelength 5.1 × 10–7 m is shone on metal X, the stopping potential is 0.9 V.

(3) The work function of metal Y is 2 eV.

A (1) and (2) only

B (1) and (3) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-E201-12.reasoning:
Threshold wavelength for X = 6.6 × 10–7 m

Light with wavelength longer than this value cannot produce photoelectric effect.

∴ (1) is correct.

When λ = 5.1 × 10–7 m,

Kmax for the photoelectrons emitted by X

= 0.9 × 10–19 J = 0.563 eV

∴ Stopping potential = 0.563 V

∴ (2) is incorrect.

By φ = hcλmax,

φ for Y = (6.63 × 10–34)(3 × 108)(6.2 × 10–7)(1.60 × 10–19) = 2 eV

∴ (3) is correct.

tb-E201-18.question:
In the photoelectric effect experiment, blue light of frequency 6.2 × 1014 Hz is directed onto the cathode. Figure g shows how the photoelectric current I varies with the p.d. V across the photocell for two different intensities of incident light. V is defined to be positive when the anode of the photocell is connected to the positive terminal of the power supply.

(a) Why is I zero when V = –1 V? (1 mark)

(b) Explain why the two curves have the same intercept on the horizontal axis. (3 marks)

(c) Find the work function (in eV) of the cathode. (2 marks)

(d) When V increases and passes a certain positive value, I reaches a constant value. What is the physical meaning of this constant value of I? (1 mark)

(e) Find the maximum KE of the photoelectrons reaching the anode when

(i) V = –0.5 V, (1 mark)

(ii) V = 2 V. (1 mark)
tb-E201-18.answer:
(a) The p.d. across the photocell is large enough to prevent all photoelectrons from reaching the anode. 1A

(b) As the incident lights with different intensities have the same frequency, the energy (hf ) of each photon is the same. 1A

This implies that the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons emitted, hence the stopping potential Vs, is also the same. 1A

Therefore, the intercepts of the two curves on the horizontal axis, indicating the values of −Vs, are the same. 1A

(c) By Kmax = eVs = hf – φ,

1 = (6.63 × 10–34)(6.2 × 1014)1.60 × 10–19 – φ 1M

φ = 1.57 eV 1A

(d) It is the current produced when all photoelectrons can reach the anode. 1A

(e) (i) Maximum KE = eVs + eV

= 1 + (–0.5)

= 0.5 eV 1A

(ii) Maximum KE = eVs + eV

= 1 + 2

= 3 eV 1A

(a) Intensity

= NhfAt

= NhcAtλ

= (1 × 1014)(6.63 × 10–34)(3 × 108)(0.05 × 0.05)(1)(550 × 10–9) 1M

= 0.0145 W m–2 1A

(b) Kmax

= hcλ – φ

= (6.63 × 10–34)(3 × 108)(550 × 10–9)(1.60 × 10–19) – 2.1 1M

(ii) E = hcλ

= (6.63 × 10–34)(3 × 108)(680 × 10–9)(1.60 × 10–19)

= 1.83 eV 1A

< φ

∴ Photoelectric effect will not occur. 1A
